description:
Automatically converts a physical SIM card (pSIM) currently active in the device into an eSIM
profile.

CRITICAL SEMANTIC RULES FOR GEMINI / BARD PLANNER:
1. DO NOT trigger or call this tool if the user's request is vague, general, or just inquires
about SIM types (e.g., "what is a physical SIM", "tell me about SIM cards").
2. DO NOT trigger this tool if the user is asking to buy a new SIM plan or check SIM
availability.
3. ONLY invoke this function if the user expresses a clear, explicit, and definitive intent to
convert their active physical carrier card into a digital eSIM profile (e.g., "convert my
SIM to eSIM", "change my physical SIM to eSIM", "make my active SIM digital").
4. If the user's intent is vague or has multiple interpretations, you MUST ask clarifying
questions (e.g., "Would you like to convert your physical SIM card to an eSIM profile?")
instead of triggering this tool.

This function initiates the physical-to-eSIM conversion flow by launching the confirmation
activity in the foreground and returns SUCCESS immediately once the activity is started.

An EsimConvertResponse representing the outcome. status can be: - "SUCCESS": The eSIM conversion confirmation flow was successfully launched in the foreground. - "FEATURE_DISABLED": The conversion capability is disabled or not supported on this device. - "NO_ACTIVE_PSIM": No active physical SIM profile was found to perform conversion from. - "CARRIER_UNSUPPORTED": The mobile network carrier of the active physical SIM card does not authorize pSIM to eSIM conversion. - "NO_WIFI": The device is not connected to WiFi. - "DEVICE_NOT_SECURE": The device does not have a secure lock screen. - "ACTIVITY_LAUNCH_FAILED": A platform-level launch crash or framework error occurred. - "NEEDS_DISAMBIGUATION": Multiple physical SIMs are active and the assistant must ask the user to select one. - "EXISTING_ESIM_WILL_BE_DISABLED": The device already has an active eSIM and is non-MEP. Activating the converted eSIM will disable the existing one. - "CONVERSION_DISABLES_OTHER_SIM": The device is in DSDS mode with two active pSIMs. Activating the eSIM will disable the physical SIM in the shared slot. - "CARRIER_RESTRICTED": Slot switching is restricted by carrier policy (e.g. Verizon).
The display name of the physical SIM profile to convert. If not provided and multiple physical SIMs are active, the function will return NEEDS_DISAMBIGUATION.
name: profileDisplayName

description:
Automatically initiates and executes the pairing flow to transfer eSIM cellular profiles from a
source mobile device (either another Android or an iOS/iPhone) onto this target Android device.

CRITICAL SEMANTIC RULES FOR GEMINI / BARD PLANNER:
1. DO NOT trigger or call this tool under any circumstances if the user's request is vague,
general, or just inquires about eSIM transfer (e.g., "can I transfer my eSIM", "how do I
move my line", "carrier transfer info").
2. DO NOT trigger this tool if the user is asking to purchase a new line or change carrier
contracts.
3. ONLY invoke this function if the user expresses a clear, explicit, and definitive intent to
migrate, transfer, or move their active eSIM plan from their old phone onto this specific
device right now (e.g., "transfer my eSIM from my old phone", "move my number from my
iPhone", "migrate my eSIM").
4. If the user's intent is vague or has multiple interpretations, you MUST ask clarifying
questions (e.g., "Would you like to transfer your eSIM profile from another phone to this
device?") instead of triggering this tool.
5. DO NOT trigger this tool if the user wants to transfer an eSIM FROM this device TO another
device. This tool only supports transferring FROM another device TO this device. If the user
wants to transfer an eSIM out of this device, you must inform them that it is not supported
directly, and they should initiate the transfer from their target (new) device instead.

This function initiates the eSIM transfer pairing flow by launching the QR pairing activity in
the foreground and returns SUCCESS immediately once the activity is started. If the user asks
to transfer eSIMs but doesn't specify whether their old phone is an Android or an iPhone, this
tool returns status "NEEDS_DEVICE_DISAMBIGUATION" along with the list of supported devices.

CONVERSATIONAL CONTRACT FOR BARD/GEMINI: When this tool returns status
"NEEDS_DEVICE_DISAMBIGUATION", you MUST present the allowed devices verbatim to the user as
options (e.g., "Are you transferring from an Android phone or an iPhone?") and ask them to
select one. Once they select, you must re-run this tool passing their choice directly.

An EsimTransferResponse representing the outcome. status can be: - "SUCCESS": The eSIM transfer pairing onboarding flow was successfully launched. - "FEATURE_DISABLED": The transfer capability is disabled or not supported on this device. When this status is returned, Gemini MUST fall back to presenting manual step-by-step text instructions to the user to transfer their eSIM from Settings. - "NEEDS_DEVICE_DISAMBIGUATION": The assistant must ask whether their old device is Android or iPhone. - "ACTIVITY_LAUNCH_FAILED": An application-level launch crash or framework error occurred.

Specifies the type of the source device: - `null` (Default): The user has NOT specified their source device type. The tool will evaluate eligibility and return "NEEDS_DEVICE_DISAMBIGUATION" if selection is required. - `false`: The user explicitly specified they are transferring from an Android device. - `true`: The user explicitly specified they are transferring from an iPhone/iOS device.
name: isIosTransfer

description:
Handles the eSIM deletion flow. It verifies that eSIM AppFunctions are enabled on the device,
then initiates the profile deletion process, returning the execution status.

If the user asks to delete profiles but multiple active eSIM profiles exist on the device and
no specific profileDisplayNames list is provided, this tool returns status
"NEEDS_DISAMBIGUATION" along with the list of all available profile names in the "profileNames"
return field.

CRITICAL SEMANTIC RULES FOR GEMINI / BARD PLANNER:
1. DO NOT trigger or call this tool under any circumstances if the user's request is vague,
general, or just inquires about cellular profiles (e.g., "what profiles are on my phone",
"can I erase my data").
2. DO NOT trigger this tool to switch, disable, or select a default profile. This tool is
strictly for PERMANENT DELETION/ERASURE of eSIM plans!
3. ONLY invoke this function if the user expresses a clear, explicit, and definitive intent to
permanently delete, erase, or remove one or more of their active eSIM carrier profiles from
their phone right now (e.g., "delete my eSIM", "erase my T-Mobile profile", "remove my eSIM
plan").
4. If the user's intent is vague or has multiple interpretations, you MUST ask clarifying
questions (e.g., "Would you like to permanently delete an eSIM profile from this device?")
instead of triggering this tool.
5. If the user wants to delete all eSIM profiles, or both profiles (when there are exactly
two), you can pass "all" or "both" as a value in the `profileDisplayNames` list. This will
instruct the tool to target all available eSIM profiles for deletion.

CONVERSATIONAL CONTRACT FOR BARD/GEMINI: When this tool returns status "NEEDS_DISAMBIGUATION",
you MUST present all the returned profile names verbatim to the user as options (e.g., "I found
multiple profiles: Carrier A, Carrier B. Which one would you like to delete?") and ask them to
select one. Never ask the user to choose without explicitly listing all returned profile
options verbatim from the "profileNames" list.

An EsimDeleteResponse representing the outcome. status can be: - "SUCCESS": The target eSIM profiles were successfully erased/deleted. - "FEATURE_DISABLED": The deletion capability is disabled or not supported on this device. When this status is returned, Gemini MUST fall back to presenting manual step-by-step text instructions to the user to delete their eSIM profile from Settings. - "NO_ESIM_PROFILE": No active eSIM profiles exist on the device to perform deletion from. - "NEEDS_DISAMBIGUATION": Multiple profiles exist and the assistant must ask the user which to delete. - "USER_CANCELED": The user explicitly canceled the deletion attempt inside the privileged dialog. - "ACTIVITY_LAUNCH_FAILED": A platform-level launch crash or framework error occurred.
Optional list of target eSIM profile display names (or nicknames) to delete. Can also contain "all" or "both" to delete all available profiles.
name: profileDisplayNames

description:
Automatically initiates and executes the privileged download and installation flow of a NEW
eSIM profile on the device.

CRITICAL SEMANTIC RULES FOR GEMINI / BARD PLANNER:
1. DO NOT trigger or call this tool under any circumstances if the user's request is vague,
general, or just inquires about eSIMs (e.g., "I want to buy an eSIM", "how does eSIM work",
"tell me about eSIMs").
2. DO NOT trigger this tool if the user is asking to purchase, search for, or browse cellular
carrier plans. This tool CANNOT buy, search for, or browse plans.
3. WARNING: If the user says "SIM" or "SIM card" without explicitly prepending "e" or "eSIM"
(e.g., "I want to setup my SIM"), the request is highly ambiguous and could refer to a
physical SIM card (pSIM). DO NOT trigger this tool for generic "SIM" requests under any
circumstances! You MUST ask clarifying questions first to confirm if they want to setup a
physical SIM or an eSIM profile!
4. ONLY invoke this function if the user expresses a clear, explicit, and definitive intent to
physically install or setup a NEW eSIM profile (with the "e" explicitly stated!) that they
have already obtained or are ready to provision on this specific device right now (e.g.,
"install eSIM now", "setup eSIM").
5. STRICT EXCLUSION FOR ACTIVATING/ENABLING EXISTING PROFILES: DO NOT invoke this function if
the user wants to "activate", "turn on", "enable", "disable", or "turn off" an eSIM profile
that is already installed or exists on the device. This tool ONLY handles setting
up/downloading NEW profiles, not toggling or activating existing ones.
6. If the user's intent is vague or has multiple interpretations, you MUST ask clarifying
questions (e.g., "Would you like to setup a new eSIM profile on this device?") instead of
triggering this tool.
7. CARRIER APP CLARIFICATION MANDATE: If the user specifies a specific carrier name along with
the setup request (e.g., "setup my Verizon eSIM", "setup T-Mobile eSIM"), you MUST present
the following warning to the user first: "We can setup your eSIM if you already have a
profile ready or a QR code to scan. However, if your carrier recommends using their
carrier-specific app for activation, you will need to perform setup from their app. Do you
want to continue?" You MUST obtain their explicit verbal confirmation ("yes", "continue",
etc.) before invoking this tool!

This function initiates the eSIM setup onboarding flow by launching the Setup Activity in the
foreground and returns SUCCESS immediately once the activity is started.

An EsimSetupResponse representing the outcome. status can be: - [EsimSetupStatus.SUCCESS]: The setup onboarding flow was successfully launched in the foreground. - [EsimSetupStatus.FEATURE_DISABLED]: The setup capability is disabled, not supported on this device, or cannot be auto-launched (e.g. active physical SIM present requiring DSDS confirmation dialog). When this status is returned, Gemini MUST fall back to presenting manual step-by-step text instructions to the user to setup their eSIM. - [EsimSetupStatus.ACTIVITY_LAUNCH_FAILED]: An application-level launch crash or framework error occurred.

Represents the metadata of relevant device settings, structured for consumption by an LLM. This
serves as the top-level response object when querying device state schema.
List of per-screen device states.

The device's locale, represented as a BCP 47 language tag.

Examples: "en-US", "fr-CA", "zh-Hans-CN".

Additional hints for the LLM to help it understand the device / device state that aren't scoped
to a specific screen.

Provides details for settings that are duplicated across multiple items. For example,
notification settings are duplicated for each app.

Each item in the list represents an "itemization type" (e.g., "package" for per-app or "sim"
for per-SIM settings). The `key` in [ItemizationType] is the itemization type, and the `values`
list contains all items of that type on the device.

For the "package" itemization type, the `values` list would contain an [ItemizationDetail] for
each app, where `key` is the package name and `value` is the user-friendly app name.

A [PerScreenMetadata] with a non-empty `itemizationTypes` refers to a generic screen whose
settings apply to every item in the corresponding list in this field.

A list that shows allowed packages for intent URI destinations (the app implementing the app
function is always allowed). The agent can use this list as filter to remove any
model-generated intent uris that don't match.

description:
Remembers any notable information or context(e.g. physical/semantic location) about a PHYSICAL item to help inventory your physical world. This function is versatile for any detail * tied to an item but is PARTICULARLY well-suited and designed for storing *where* you have placed personal belongings like passports, keys, wallets, car, phone, documents etc., within the `Items` tab of FindHub.

This function is item-centric. This differs from the general note-saving function by focusing on object location rather than arbitrary text like phone numbers, addresses, or general notes.

Use this function as the default for any "remember where I put X" or "remember this about X" type of requests for PHYSICAL TANGIBLE objects. Prime Examples (Location):

  • Remember that the sunglasses (personal item) are above the fireplace (location).
  • Remember that my passport (personal item) in the desk (location).
  • Remember that I parked the car (personal item) in the neighboring lot (location) today.
  • I left the keys (personal item) on the kitchen counter (location).
generatedEmoji: The AI agent should generate the best single emoji that best describes the main noun of each string. AVOID supplying more than one emoji.
  • INPUT: "passport"

    BAD OUTPUT: "passport" reasoning: not an emoji

    GOOD OUTPUT: "🛂"

  • INPUT: "super ultra fast computer"

    BAD OUTPUT: "⚡" reasoning: does not describe main noun

    GOOD OUTPUT: "💻"

  • INPUT: "surfboard"

    BAD OUTPUT: "🏄‍♂️🌊" reasoning: more than one emoji

    GOOD OUTPUT: "🏄‍♂️"

generatedItemCategories: The AI agent should provide up to 3 categories from the provided list that would best describe the personalItem provided by the user. If the item does not fit into any of these categories, return null. ONLY select categories from this list:
  • "Tools"
  • "Electronics"
  • "Travel"
  • "Documents"
  • "Office supplies"
  • "Kitchenware"
  • "Storage"
  • "Clothing"
  • "Safety"
  • "Sports"
  • "Accessories"
  • "Medical"
  • "Valuables"
  • "Gardening"
  • "Hobbies"
  • "Food"
  • INPUT: "passport"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Photos"] reasoning: not a category in the list

    GOOD OUTPUT: ["Documents", "Travel", "Identification"]

  • INPUT: "super ultra fast computer"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Sports"] reasoning: bad category fit

    GOOD OUTPUT: ["Electronics"]

  • INPUT: "cat toy"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Hobbies"] reasoning: bad category fit

    GOOD OUTPUT: null reasoning: cat toy does not fit into any of the categories

recognizedSpaces: The AI agent should return a list of spaces or Spaces from the provided list below that are identified within the location provided by the user. ONLY select Spaces from this list. These will be used to group and filter items in specific locations. If the location provided by the user does not fit into any of these Spaces, return null.
  • "Kitchen"
  • "Living room"
  • "Bedroom"
  • "Bathroom"
  • "Garage"
  • "Office"
  • "Dining room"
  • "Laundry room"
  • "Closet"
  • "Basement"
  • "Attic"
  • "Pantry"
  • "Entryway"
  • "Nursery"
  • "Gym"
  • "Workshop"
  • "Library"
  • "Outside"
  • "Hallway"
  • "Vehicle"
  • INPUT: "on counter in kitchen"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Counter"] reasoning: not in list

    GOOD OUTPUT: ["Kitchen"] reasoning: in list and explicitly mentioned.

  • INPUT: "in my closet in the bedroom"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Closet"] reasoning: missing another mentioned bedroom

    GOOD OUTPUT: ["Closet", "Bedroom"] reasoning: both are in list and fit context.

  • INPUT: "on the bed"

    BAD OUTPUT: null reasoning: can deduce space to be bedroom

    GOOD OUTPUT: ["Bedroom"] reasoning: It is a reasonable deduction to assume the mentioned bed is in a bedroom.

  • INPUT: "on the table"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Dining room"] reasoning: tables could be in multiple spaces

    GOOD OUTPUT: null reasoning: it is not clear which space the table is in, therefore a space should not be deduced.

  • INPUT: "in my car"

    BAD OUTPUT: ["Garage"] reasoning: "car" is not a room, but a vehicle

    GOOD OUTPUT: ["Vehicle"]

  • Where are my sunglasses?
  • Do you know where is my passport?
  • Where are my keys?
If [MemoryFunctions.RecallLocationResponse.lastUpdatedDate] is null, then the agent should only provide the location of the object. If [MemoryFunctions.RecallLocationResponse.lastUpdatedDate] is not null, then the agent should provide the location of the object and the date it was last updated, prefaced by "It was last updated on". Example responses:
  • RecallLocationResponse(location = "above the fireplace", lastUpdatedDate = null), GOOD RESPONSE: "The sunglasses are above the fireplace."
  • GOOD RESPONSE: RecallLocationResponse(location = "in your desk", lastUpdatedDate = "January 1, 2024"), GOOD RESPONSE: "You stored your passport in your desk. It was last updated on January 1, 2024."

**Fuzzy Fallback Protocol (Crucial LLM Instruction):** If this function returns a location containing "No information available about" or empty results, the user's query might be fuzzy, using a synonym, or referring to a category of objects (e.g., asking for "keys" when "yellow keys" is stored, or "ski gear" when "ski boots", "skis", and "poles" is stored). The agent **MUST** fall back to calling [getAllMemoriesForDisambiguation] to load the full list of memories, perform semantic reasoning to find the matching items, and synthesize a natural consolidated response.

description:
Returns a list of all personal physical items and their locations stored in the FindHub Memory.

This is designed specifically to support advanced semantic reasoning, fuzzy substring matching, synonym expansion, and category groupings that cannot be resolved by the simple exact matching of [recallLocation].

Use this function as the primary tool or fallback when the user's query is vague, contains synonyms, asks for a category/group of objects, or if [recallLocation] returns no information. Prime Examples (LLM Processing Protocol):

  • **Fuzzy Substring Matching:** User query: "Where are my keys?" Stored memories: [{"item": "yellow keys", "location": "in drawer"}, {"item": "red keys", "location": "in box"}] Action: Gemini calls this method, parses the list, performs substring matches for "keys", finds both "yellow keys" and "red keys", and consolidates them into a natural response: "Your yellow keys are in the drawer and red keys are in the box."
  • **Synonym Resolution & Brand-to-Generic Mappings:** User query: "Where are my tissues?" or "Do I have any bandages?" Stored memories: [{"item": "napkins", "location": "in the pantry"}, {"item": "Kleenex", "location": "in the living room"}, {"item": "Band-Aids", "location": "in the bathroom cabinet"}] Action: Gemini calls this method, recognizes "napkins" as a synonym for "tissues", maps brand names to their generic counterpart (e.g., "Kleenex" to "tissues", "Band-Aids" to "bandages"), and lists all relevant details to the user.
  • **Smart Brand Translations:** User query: "Where are my plastic food containers?" or "where did I stash the sticky notes?" Stored memories: [{"item": "Tupperware", "location": "in the kitchen cupboard"}, {"item": "Post-it notes", "location": "on the desk"}] Action: Gemini calls this method and performs semantic reasoning to translate generic items to stored popular brand representations (Tupperware vs food containers, Post-it notes vs sticky notes).
  • **Spelling, Nicknames & Phonetic Variations:** User query: "Where are Alyce's shoes?" or "Where is Ed's jacket?" Stored memories: [{"item": "Alice's shoes", "location": "by the door"}, {"item": "Edward's jacket", "location": "on the hook"}, {"item": "Knight statue", "location": "on the table"}] Action: Gemini calls this method, resolves phonetic/spelling variations (Alice vs Alyce, Knight vs Night) and common abbreviations (Ed vs Edward), and responds accordingly.
  • **Category/Grouping Expansion:** User query: "Where is my ski gear?" Stored memories: [{"item": "skis", "location": "in garage"}, {"item": "poles", "location": "in garage"}, {"item": "skiboots", "location": "in closet"}] Action: Gemini calls this method, groups all stored items related to "ski gear", and responds: "Your skis and poles are in the garage, and your skiboots are in the closet."
  • **Fallback on Miss:** User query: "Where is my wallet?" Action: Gemini calls `recallLocation(personalItem = "wallet")` -> returns "No information available". Fallback Action: Gemini calls this method to inspect all memories, searches for near matches or related terms (e.g., "card holder"), and presents relevant results.
